newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo 1996 c/a deficit seen at $1.3-1.4 bln - IEN.
newsitem.headline: Yugo 1996 c/a deficit seen at $1.3-1.4 bln - IEN.

text.p: Yugoslavia's current account deficit will reach some $1.4 billion at the end of 1996, and its trade gap $1.85 billion, an economic institute said in its latest monthly report.
"Yugoslavia will have a $1.3 billion or $1.4 billion current account deficit in 1996," Stojan Stamenkovic of the Institute of Economic Sciences (IEN) told Reuters on Wednesday.

Stamenkovic said the level of the current account deficit depended on services sector performance. But he cautioned that the third segment of the current account -- interest rates -- was still not included, because interest payments will begin in 1997.
"It is possible for the services sector to produce a surplus of up to $250 million, mainly from transport and tourism," Stamenkovic said.
Another $200 million could come from a barter deal with China, but this remains uncertain, he added.
"However, all this will help cut the current account deficit to up to $1.4 billion," Stamenkovic said.
The Trade gap, as the key deficit generator, was expected to range between $1.8 billion and $1.9 billion, he said.
The September trade deficit stood at $1.396 billion, with imports reaching $2.65 billion and exports $1.26 billion.
The trade gap was expected to start narrowing due to limited sources for its financing and a possible increase of exports through the barter with China, IEN report said.
The $1 billion barter deal with China, signed mid-March, involves Serbia importing crude and oil products in exchange for exports of fertiliser, chemicals and food.
Referring to the current account data, Stamenkovic said they were processed by the central bank, but for some reason kept confidential.
Former Yugoslavia ran its highest current account deficit of $3.7 billion in 1979.
In 1990, former Yugoslavia's current account balance was around $2 billion in the red, Stamenkovic said.
"This shows how big our 1996 current account deficit will be, because it will account for two thirds of the total exports," Stamenkovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
